conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee, one of the vascular surgery team. You've been admitted tonight because of the ulcers on your left foot and the blockage we saw in your leg artery last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I remember. The angiogram showed a bad blockage in my left leg, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. It's a near-occlusive lesion in the left superficial femoral artery. We’re planning to fix that with a procedure called an endarterectomy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that like a bypass? I thought I was getting a bypass.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We initially planned a bypass using your own vein, but we need to check first if the vein is usable. That’s why we’re doing a vein mapping ultrasound tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. And what about my blood thinner? I’m on Coumadin for my mechanical valve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. We’re stopping your Coumadin for now and starting a heparin drip. That’s safer around surgery. We’ll restart Coumadin after the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the heparin will be adjusted based on my blood tests?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll monitor your PTT and adjust the drip to keep it in the right range. Once your INR is back up to 3.0–3.5, we’ll stop the heparin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll need dialysis too—usually on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve scheduled dialysis for tomorrow. The transplant nephrology team will be following you as well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your vein mapping ultrasound was done this morning. The greater saphenous vein in your left leg is patent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So we can use it for the bypass?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll find out during surgery. Sometimes that vein was used in prior heart surgery and might not be available.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had a CABG years ago—could they have taken it then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. If it was harvested, we’ll have to use a different approach. But we have a backup plan—endarterectomy with patch angioplasty.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, as long as the blood flow gets fixed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You just finished dialysis. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little tired, but okay. No cramps this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring your labs, especially potassium and fluid status.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning your surgery for tomorrow morning. Any questions before then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just—what exactly is an endarterectomy?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We open the artery and remove the plaque buildup. Then we sew in a patch to keep it open. It’s a direct way to fix the blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll be in the ICU after?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the VICU for one night, just to monitor your heart and circulation closely, given your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, you're back from surgery. The procedure went well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Did you use my vein for the bypass?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We explored the greater saphenous vein, but it was tied off—likely used in your prior CABG. So instead, we did a femoral endarterectomy with patch angioplasty.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that as good as a bypass?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: For your type of blockage, yes. It restores blood flow and should help your foot ulcers heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’m glad it’s done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is now 2.8. We’re still running the heparin drip but getting close to stopping it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When will I be back on Coumadin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re already on it—4 mg daily. Once your INR hits 3.0–3.5 and stays there, we’ll stop the heparin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—am I back on all of them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, including tacrolimus, sirolimus, and aspirin. The transplant team reviewed everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The podiatry team cultured your foot ulcer today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Was there an infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The culture grew coagulase-negative staph. It’s a common skin bacterium, but we’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Do I need different antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. You’re already on IV vancomycin on dialysis days, which covers it. We’ll continue that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your latest labs show your INR is now 3.9.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that too high?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s slightly above our target of 3.0–3.5, but since we’re stopping the heparin today, it should stabilize.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. Can I start walking more?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the physical therapist saw you today. You’re doing well. They recommend home physical therapy after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll need help at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, home nursing and physical therapy. You’ll need help with wound checks and mobility at first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re healing well. The incision looks clean, no signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my foot ulcer?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Podiatry says it’s stable. Improved blood flow should help it heal over time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on a special diet too, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 2 grams sodium and 2 grams potassium. It’s important for your heart and kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll keep that up at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call us if you have fever over 100.5, increased pain, redness spreading from the incision, or drainage that’s yellow or green.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And activity?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can walk and go up and down stairs, but no heavy lifting—nothing over five pounds—for two weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I shower?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, let water run over the incision, pat dry. No soaking in a tub yet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. We’ve arranged home nursing, physical therapy, and your follow-up with Dr. Patel in two weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I keep taking Coumadin, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 4 mg daily. Continue all your other meds too—especially the transplant and dialysis ones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home today. The team is proud of your progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Remember: elevate your leg when sitting, eat small frequent meals, and keep up with your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And call if anything seems off.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your incision can stay uncovered unless there’s drainage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Just a dry dressing if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’re all set.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Rest well and keep building your strength.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.
